newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on USDA report.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed sharply lower with the market again hit by Friday's USDA October crop production report, traders said.
Fund selling was noted with nearly ideal U.S. harvest weather over the weekend also hitting prices, they said.
"There was spillover from the crop report and the good harvest weather weighed on it," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA Friday estimated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.346 billion bushels, above average trade expectations for 2.287 billion.
Late fund selling included Prudential Securities, Smith Barney, Refco Inc and Tenco Inc, traders said.
New crop November set a session low of $6.82 in late trading, a 10 month low and the lowest level for that contract since December 8, 1995.
"There was more liquidation on good harvest weather and it now looks like a few more days of good weather," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybeans closed four to 12-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down 11-3/4 at $6.88-1/2. January was down 12-3/4 at $6.94-1/4.
The active new crop November contract has fallen roughly $1.37 per bushel, or about 16-1/2 percent of its value, since its contract high of $8.25 per bushel was notched July 12.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report revealed that as of October 8 non-commercials were long soybeans by 207.315 million bushels and short by 68.170 million, indicating the potential for more fund long liquidation.

"The CFTC report gives a clear indication there still is more long liquidation to come, especially in soybeans and in meal," a trader said. Also "there are big fears China may cancel their bean or meal purchases."
There were reports Monday in the cash market that China may have cancelled 150,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 75,000 contracts, down from 88,140 Friday, according to the CBOT.

On the day, Tenco Inc sold six million bushels of November, Merrill Lynch Futures sold 7.5 million November and Prudential Securities sold three million November and sold three million January, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 40,000, down from 56,533 Friday.
Smith Barney bought 3,000 January $7.00 puts and sold 3,000 January $6.75 puts at 11-1/2 cents and bought 500 January $7.25 puts and sold 500 January $6.75 puts at 29 to 30 cents, traders said.
